title: After Finishing My Study Abroad in Gdansk
paragraphs: From March to July this year I studied abroad at the Medical University of Gdansk (Akademia Medyczna w Gdansku) in Poland. My clerkships were two weeks each in obstetrics, palliative medicine, gastrointestinal surgery, gastroenterology, urology, pediatrics and dermatology. Sometimes I was in the same group as exchange students from EU countries, or just with 小野寺, who studied abroad with me, but most of the time I went to the department alone and received careful guidance. As in the hospital clerkships at Nagoya University, some departments were enthusiastic about teaching students and others were less so, but I enjoyed the clerkship every time. In the evenings after the hospital clerkship, I also trained with the judo club of a local sports university, the Akademia Wychowania Fizycznego i Sportu w Gdansku (AWFiS Gdansk). This judo club is the strongest club in the country, ranked first in Poland for both men and women, and I had the valuable experience, unthinkable in Japan, of training with Olympic and international representative players. Naturally, the training was very hard and strict, but I spent fulfilling days. Life in Gdansk was very comfortable. The dormitory near the university was spacious, with private rooms, clean and free of charge. In addition, the Polish food I ate in the dormitory canteen and in town was delicious, plentiful and cheap, and I was always satisfied. The Eastern European climate from spring to summer was also pleasant. Everything about this study abroad was fresh and a very good experience. My first life in Eastern Europe, a hospital clerkship abroad, living and drinking with medical students from other countries, a judo life at a sports university that I had not expected at all before going, drinking and going out with the students of the sports university and with working judo players, traveling within the country and abroad on days off, and everything else about the study abroad was fun. Even being scolded harshly by doctors at the hospital has now become a good memory. Finally, from the bottom of my heart I thank Dr. 伊藤 and Dr. 小林, who sent a failure like me abroad, the office staff, Dr. 若林 who looked after me in Gdansk, his wife, the members of the laboratory, the teachers of the medical university and the sports university, the seniors of "Gdansk 若林 Group" who held a send-off party and a return report meeting and gave me various advice, 小野寺 who studied abroad with me, and everyone who helped me. Thank you very much.
